title: AutoSTF: Decoupled Neural Architecture Search for Cost-Effective Automated Spatio-Temporal Forecasting

problem.claim: Spatio-temporal forecasting supports smart city applications and requires modeling complex spatio-temporal dependencies.

gap.claim: Existing automated approaches incur expensive neural architecture search overhead, limiting practical use and fine-grained exploration of spatio-temporal operators.

contributions.claim: AutoSTF is a decoupled automatic neural architecture search framework for cost-effective automated spatio-temporal forecasting.
The framework separates temporal and spatial search spaces and uses representation compression and parameter sharing to reduce parameter explosion and search overhead.
The framework introduces a multi-patch transfer module and finer-grained layer-wise spatial dependency search.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on eight datasets are reported to demonstrate superiority in accuracy and efficiency.
The method is reported to achieve up to 13.48x speed-up over state-of-the-art automated spatio-temporal forecasting methods while maintaining the best forecasting accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spatio-temporal forecasting is positioned as important for smart city applications.
Automated forecasting methods search neural architectures, but their search overhead limits practical and fine-grained use.
AutoSTF decouples search spaces, adds efficiency mechanisms, and expands temporal and spatial dependency modeling.
The authors report results on eight datasets and provide source code and data.

source_observation.claim: Decoupling a mixed architecture search space into temporal and spatial components, combined with compression and parameter sharing, is reported to reduce search cost.

interpretation.claim: Separating coupled search dimensions may improve computational scalability while preserving room for more targeted dependency modeling.

application.claim: For automated spatio-temporal forecasting, consider modular search over temporal and spatial operators with shared or compressed representations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers to other tasks, search spaces, or computational settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the eight datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental protocols.
The abstract does not provide search costs, hardware settings, ablation results, or independent verification.
The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the reported 13.48x speed-up and best accuracy were measured.
